query: FeCoNi is an fcc alloy with high saturation magnetization and a low coercive field. Earlier studies examined the high-entropy alloys FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt, but both exhibited soft ferromagnetism. A qualifying high-entropy alloy must have an almost equiatomic multicomponent composition and configurational entropy of at least 1.0R. Subject to these constraints, what single intervention could produce a FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy with greater coercivity than the prior derivatives? Present one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to an appropriate FeCoNi-based baseline, defines the conditions over which it should apply, cites supporting observations from earlier work, and proposes a discriminating experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Rapid thermal annealing (RTA) of an equiatomic FeCoNi high-entropy alloy can induce atomic reordering that transforms the initial fcc soft-magnetic phase into an ordered microstructure with enhanced magnetic anisotropy and substantially increased coercivity.
generation.material_initial_state: As-deposited, equiatomic FeCoNi high-entropy alloy films (or bulk materials) in a single fcc phase exhibiting soft ferromagnetism with low coercivity (on the order of 10 Oe).
generation.intervention: Apply a controlled rapid thermal annealing (RTA) treatment at an optimized high temperature for a short time.
generation.conditions: RTA performed under an inert atmosphere at temperatures high enough (e.g., >500°C) to promote atomic diffusion but short enough in duration (seconds to minutes) to preserve overall equiatomic composition and high configurational entropy.
generation.structural_mediator: Induction of an ordered phase (e.g., an L10-like structure) or formation of nanoscale ordered domains within the fcc matrix that enhance magnetic anisotropy and provide effective domain wall pinning.
generation.mechanism: RTA accelerates atomic mobility and drives a reordering process. This reordering can lead to the emergence of an ordered intermetallic microstructure that increases magnetic anisotropy and resistance to domain wall motion, thereby enhancing coercivity compared to the disordered state.
generation.predicted_outcome: Post-RTA, the FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy is expected to exhibit a coercivity significantly higher (potentially 10× to 1000× increase) than the as-deposited soft ferromagnetic baseline, overcoming the soft-ferromagnetism observed in prior FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt derivatives.
generation.baseline: The as-deposited FeCoNi-based alloy films or bulk materials, which form a single fcc phase with low coercivity.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is applicable to equiatomic, multicomponent FeCoNi-based alloys that meet the minimum configurational entropy requirement (≈1.0R); it assumes that the RTA conditions are finely tuned to induce ordering without leading to deleterious phase segregation or loss of homogeneity.
generation.uncertainty: It remains uncertain whether the pure FeCoNi high-entropy system (without additional anisotropy-promoting elements) will form the same degree of ordered structure—and thus achieve coercivity enhancements—as seen in systems that have incorporated elements like Pt during annealing.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare equiatomic FeCoNi alloy films (or bulk samples) using sputtering, then split them into two groups. Subject one group to RTA under carefully controlled conditions (e.g., >500°C for a short duration in an inert atmosphere) while keeping the other group as-deposited. Use structural characterization (e.g., X-ray diffraction, transmission electron microscopy) to check for the development of ordered phases and magnetic measurements (via SQUID or VSM) to assess changes in coercivity.
measurements: X-ray diffraction (XRD) to identify the emergence of ordered (L10-like) phases
Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) to observe nanoscale ordering
Magnetometry (SQUID, VSM) to measure coercivity and overall magnetic hysteresis
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the RTA-treated samples do not exhibit both clear signatures of atomic ordering (e.g., L10 phase peaks or ordered domains) and a statistically significant increase in coercivity (e.g., less than a 10× increase) compared to the as-deposited baseline, then the hypothesis is considered falsified.

## Abstract
AbstractThe vast high entropy alloy (HEA) composition space is promising for discovery of new material phases with unique properties. This study explores the potential to achieve rare‐earth‐free high magnetic anisotropy materials in single‐phase HEA thin films. Thin films of FeCoNiMnCu sputtered on thermally oxidized Si/SiO2 substrates at room temperature are magnetically soft, with a coercivity on the order of 10 Oe. After post‐deposition rapid thermal annealing (RTA), the films exhibit a single face‐centered‐cubic phase, with an almost 40‐fold increase in coercivity. Inclusion of 50 at.% Pt in the film leads to ordering of a single L10 high entropy intermetallic phase after RTA, along with high magnetic anisotropy and 3 orders of magnitude coercivity increase. These results demonstrate a promising HEA approach to achieve high magnetic anisotropy materials using RTA.Keywords: high entropy alloy, magnetic anisotropy, rapid thermal annealing High entropy alloy (HEA) thin films are explored to achieve high magnetic anisotropy phases.
